question: Under G.S. 93A-13 and Rule A.0104(a), agency agreements for brokerage services in North Carolina must be:
choice_a: In writing and signed by the parties, for both sales and lease transactions
choice_b: Oral only, to avoid excessive paperwork
choice_c: In writing only for sales transactions, never for leases
choice_d: Notarized in all cases
explanation: Rule A.0104(a) requires all agency agreements for brokerage services, in both sales and lease transactions, to be in writing and signed by the parties.

question: Rule A.0104(a) requires an agency agreement with a property owner (seller or lessor) to be in writing:
choice_a: Within 30 days after the broker begins providing services
choice_b: Prior to the broker providing any services
choice_c: Only after the property has been shown to prospective buyers
choice_d: Only if the property is priced above $200,000
explanation: Rule A.0104(a) requires agency agreements with property owners (sellers and lessors) of any type of property to be in writing prior to the broker providing any services.

question: Under Rule A.0104(a), an oral buyer/tenant agency agreement, if allowed, must be:
choice_a: Exclusive and for a fixed multi-year term
choice_b: Reduced to writing within 24 hours of formation
choice_c: Non-exclusive and for an indefinite period, terminable by the client at any time
choice_d: Approved in advance by the Real Estate Commission
explanation: An oral buyer/tenant agency agreement must be 'non-exclusive' and for an indefinite period, terminable by the client at any time -- it must be reduced to writing no later than when any party makes an offer.

question: By what point must an oral buyer agency agreement be reduced to writing?
choice_a: Only after closing
choice_b: Within 90 days of first contact
choice_c: It never needs to be reduced to writing
choice_d: No later than the time either party to the transaction extends an offer to the other
explanation: The agent must obtain a written buyer/tenant agency agreement from the client not later than the time either party to the transaction extends an offer to the other.

question: Which required provision must every written agency agreement contain regarding non-discrimination, per Rule A.0104(b)?
choice_a: A statement that brokerage activities will be conducted without respect to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, handicap, or familial status, set forth in a clear and conspicuous manner
choice_b: A waiver of fair housing protections
choice_c: A statement limiting the agreement to United States citizens
choice_d: No such provision is required
explanation: Every written agency agreement must contain the Rule A.0104(b) non-discrimination provision, set forth clearly and conspicuously, distinguishing it from other provisions of the agreement.

question: What must every written agency agreement include regarding the licensee who signs it?
choice_a: The licensee's home address
choice_b: The license number of the individual licensee who signs the agreement
choice_c: The licensee's continuing education transcript
choice_d: A photograph of the licensee
explanation: Every written agency agreement must include the license number of the individual licensee who signs the agreement.

question: A buyer refuses to sign a written buyer agency agreement before making an offer. May the agent, without any further steps, switch to working with that buyer as a seller's subagent?
choice_a: Yes, automatically
choice_b: Yes, as long as the buyer is informed verbally at closing
choice_c: No - the agent may not continue as the buyer's agent, and may only switch to seller's subagent after fully advising the buyer of the consequences, obtaining the buyer's consent, and obtaining the seller's/listing firm's consent
choice_d: No - the transaction must be cancelled entirely
explanation: If the buyer will not sign a written buyer agency agreement, the agent may not continue to work as the buyer's agent, and may only switch to acting as seller's subagent after (1) fully advising the buyer of the consequences, (2) obtaining the buyer's consent, and (3) obtaining the consent of the seller and listing firm.

question: The Rule A.0104(c) agency disclosure requirement (providing the 'Working with Real Estate Agents' disclosure) applies to:
choice_a: Both sales and lease transactions equally
choice_b: Commercial transactions only
choice_c: Lease transactions only
choice_d: Sales transactions only
explanation: While Rule A.0104(a) requires all agency agreements (sales or lease) to be in writing, the Rule A.0104(c) agency disclosure requirement applies only to sales transactions.

question: Under Rule A.0104(c), is it sufficient for an agent to satisfy the agency disclosure requirement merely by handing a prospective buyer or seller the 'Working with Real Estate Agents' form to read?
choice_a: No - the agent must review the contents with the prospective buyer or seller and reach agreement on the agency relationship
choice_b: Yes, handing over the form alone fully satisfies the requirement
choice_c: Yes, but only if the form is notarized
choice_d: No such form exists in North Carolina
explanation: The obligation is not satisfied merely by handing the prospective seller or buyer the form to read -- the agent must review the contents with them and reach agreement regarding their agency relationship.

question: 'First substantial contact' with a prospective buyer, triggering the agency disclosure requirement, typically occurs when:
choice_a: The buyer first calls the listing phone number
choice_b: A discussion begins to focus on the buyer's specific property needs, desires, or financial situation
choice_c: The buyer signs a purchase contract
choice_d: The property closes
explanation: 'First substantial contact' occurs at the point when a discussion with a prospective buyer begins to focus on the buyer's specific property needs and desires or on the buyer's financial situation.

question: If first substantial contact with a buyer occurs by telephone where written disclosure isn't practical, what must the agent do?
choice_a: Nothing until the next in-person meeting
choice_b: Wait until closing to disclose
choice_c: Immediately disclose by similar means whom they represent, then mail or transmit the written disclosure no later than three days from first substantial contact
choice_d: Disclosure requirements do not apply to phone contact
explanation: If first substantial contact occurs by phone or electronic communication where written disclosure isn't practical, the agent must immediately disclose by similar means whom they represent, and mail or transmit a written disclosure no later than three days from first substantial contact.

question: A buyer's agent must disclose their agency status to a seller or seller's agent at 'initial contact.' By when must this be confirmed in writing?
choice_a: Only if the seller requests it
choice_b: Within 30 days of closing
choice_c: It never needs to be in writing
choice_d: No later than the time of delivery of an offer to purchase (except in auction transactions)
explanation: The initial disclosure to a seller/seller's agent may be oral, but written confirmation must be made no later than the time of delivery of an offer to purchase, except in auction sale transactions.
source_note: Disclosure of Agency Status by Buyers' Agents [Rule A.0104(f)]

question: Rule A.0112(a)(19) requires that any preprinted offer to purchase and contract form include a provision for:
choice_a: Confirmation of agency status by each real estate agent (and firm) involved in the transaction
choice_b: Waiving all agency disclosure requirements
choice_c: A blank space for the Commission's signature
choice_d: A guarantee of the property's condition
explanation: Commission Rule A.0112(a)(19) requires that any preprinted offer to purchase and contract form used by an agent include a provision confirming agency status by each real estate agent (and firm) involved in the transaction.

question: Under Rule A.0104(d), consent to dual agency must generally be obtained from all parties:
choice_a: Only after closing
choice_b: Prior to the agent undertaking to represent those parties as a dual agent, for both sales and lease/rental transactions
choice_c: Only for sales transactions, never leases
choice_d: Only if requested by one party's attorney
explanation: Rule A.0104(d) requires an agent to obtain the written authority of all parties prior to undertaking to represent those parties as a dual agent -- this requirement applies to both sales and lease/rental transactions.

question: When a buyer/tenant is represented under a permitted oral agency agreement, by when must written authority for dual agency be obtained?
choice_a: It is never required in this situation
choice_b: Within one year of the oral agreement
choice_c: No later than the time one of the represented parties makes an offer to purchase, sell, rent, lease, or exchange real estate to the other party
choice_d: Immediately at first contact, with no exceptions
explanation: For a buyer/tenant represented under an oral agency agreement, written authority for dual agency must be obtained no later than when one of the parties represented by the dual agent makes an offer to the other party.

question: Under the auction sales exemption in Rule A.0104(g), which agency disclosure provisions do NOT apply to licensees representing sellers in auction sales transactions?
choice_a: Only the written agreement requirement
choice_b: The entire License Law
choice_c: Only the non-discrimination provision
choice_d: Paragraphs (c), (d), and (e) of Rule A.0104
explanation: Paragraph (g) of Rule A.0104 provides that paragraphs (c), (d), and (e) of the Rule -- disclosure, dual agency consent, and seller's agent disclosure -- do not apply to licensees representing sellers in auction sales transactions.

question: If a buyer is represented by an agent in an auction sale, when must that buyer's agent provide the seller with written confirmation of representing the buyer?
choice_a: No later than the time of execution of a written agreement memorializing the buyer's contract to purchase
choice_b: Immediately upon entering the auction house
choice_c: This confirmation is never required in auction sales
choice_d: Only after the auction concludes and payment clears
explanation: Paragraph (h) of Rule A.0104 provides that a buyer's agent in an auction sale shall, no later than the time of execution of a written agreement memorializing the buyer's contract to purchase, provide the seller or seller's agent with a written confirmation that they represent the buyer.

question: Under Rule A.0104(i), if one agent of a firm represents a buyer client and another agent of the SAME firm represents a seller client in a transaction between those two clients, what is the agency status of the firm?
choice_a: The firm is not considered an agent at all
choice_b: The firm is a dual agent, and all licensees affiliated with the firm are also considered dual agents of those parties in that transaction
choice_c: Only the two individual agents are affected; the firm itself has no agency status
choice_d: The firm must immediately terminate both agency agreements
explanation: A firm which represents more than one party in the same real estate sales transaction is a dual agent, and because the firm functions through its associated agents, all licensees affiliated with that firm are also dual agents of those parties in that transaction.
source_note: Dual Agency Status of Firm [Rule A.0104(i)]

question: What is 'designated agency' as authorized by Rule A.0104, paragraphs (j)-(m)?
choice_a: A prohibition on all forms of dual agency
choice_b: A rule requiring two different firms to split a commission
choice_c: Appointing individual agent(s) within a firm to represent only the seller's interests and a different individual agent(s) to represent only the buyer's interests in an in-house dual agency situation
choice_d: A license category for brokers who only handle designated (assigned) territories
explanation: Designated agency involves appointing or 'designating' an individual agent(s) in a firm to represent only the interests of the seller and another individual agent(s) to represent only the interests of the buyer when a firm has an in-house dual agency situation.

question: What is the principal advantage of designated agency over 'standard' dual agency?
choice_a: It eliminates the need for any written agreements
choice_b: It removes the need for agency disclosure
choice_c: It allows the firm to charge a higher commission
choice_d: Each client receives fuller representation/advocacy from their designated agent, unlike a standard dual agent who must remain completely neutral
explanation: In standard dual agency, client advocacy is essentially lost because the dual agent may not advocate for one client to the detriment of the other and must remain neutral; designated agency returns advocacy to each client's designated agent.

question: Under Rule A.0104(n), what may an individual dual agent's written dual agency agreement authorize regarding confidential information?
choice_a: The agent to NOT disclose certain confidential information about one party to the other party without permission from the party about whom the information pertains
choice_b: Automatic disclosure of all information to both parties
choice_c: The agent to sell confidential information to third parties
choice_d: Nothing -- confidentiality provisions are prohibited
explanation: Paragraph (n) authorizes individual dual agents to include in the dual agency agreement a provision authorizing the agent not to disclose certain confidential information about one party to the other party without permission.
source_note: Dual Agency by Individual Agent [Rule A.0104(n)]

question: Under Rule A.0104(o), may a broker who has an ownership interest in a property represent a buyer of that property?
choice_a: Yes, without restriction
choice_b: Generally no, except a broker selling commercial real estate with less than 25% ownership interest may represent the buyer if the buyer consents after full written disclosure of the ownership interest
choice_c: Yes, but only for residential properties
choice_d: Only if the broker discloses the interest verbally
explanation: Rule A.0104(o) prohibits a broker selling property in which they have an ownership interest from representing a buyer of that property, except that a broker selling commercial real estate with less than 25% ownership interest may represent a buyer who consents after full written disclosure.
source_note: Brokers As Parties to Transactions [Rule A.0104(o)]

question: Under Rule A.0104(p), before a listing broker may purchase a property they themselves listed, what must occur?
choice_a: Nothing special is required
choice_b: Only a verbal disclosure at closing is required
choice_c: The broker must first disclose in writing that a potential conflict of interest exists and that the seller may want to seek independent counsel, and must terminate or transfer the listing before entering a purchase contract
choice_d: The Real Estate Commission must approve the purchase in advance
explanation: Rule A.0104(p) prohibits a listing broker or firm from purchasing a listed property unless they first disclose in writing that a potential conflict of interest exists and the seller may want independent counsel; the listing broker/firm must then terminate the listing or transfer it to another broker before entering a purchase contract.
source_note: Brokers As Parties to Transactions [Rule A.0104(p)]

question: For a landlord agency agreement to procure tenants, is automatic renewal permitted?
choice_a: No, automatic renewal is never permitted for any agency agreement
choice_b: Only if approved by the Real Estate Commission each year
choice_c: Yes, with no termination rights for the landlord at all
choice_d: Yes -- this is a specific exception allowing automatic renewal, so long as the landlord may terminate with notice at the end of any contract or renewal period
explanation: While every written agency agreement must generally terminate without prior notice at the expiration of a definite period, an exception allows an agency agreement between a broker and landlord to procure tenants to allow for automatic renewal so long as the landlord may terminate with notice at the end of any contract or renewal period.
